newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Sept 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Sept 30.

text.p: Chrysler Corp and the United Automobile Workers union reached a three-year contract similar to the one that the union negotiated with Ford Motor Co earlier this month, the Wall Street Journal reported Monday, adding that the union was to go to General Motors Corp next.

* The U.S. House of Representatives approved deep changes to securities laws that would end local scrutiny of mutual funds and reduce borrowing costs for Wall Street firms. The Senate is also expected to approve the bill, which the President Bill Clinton's administration supports.
* The founder of the New Era Foundation was named in an 82-count federal indictment. John G. Bennett Jr was accused of defrauding charitable groups and individuals of $135 million.
* ADM agreed to settle separate lawsuits filed by shareholders and citric-acid customers for a total of $65 million.
* PepsiCo Inc announced a $2-billion-a-year share buyback program as part of its plan to bring its international operations back on track.

* A U.S. federal court temporarily suspended the Federal Communications Commission's order to dissolve the country's local telephone monopolies. A hearing is set for Thursday and a ruling on whether to grant a permanent stay is expected soon afterwards.
* The U.S. Department of Defense approved full production of Northrop Grumman Corp's $9.4 billion "Joint Stars" surveillance plane program.
* Time Warner Inc plans to tell major shareholders this week that it will try to reduce its investment in the cable business.
* Ben & Jerry's Homemade Inc chief executive officer resigned in light of disagreements with the ice-cream maker's founders.
* Botson Edison and C-TEC Corp agreed to invest $300 million in an interactive data network in the Boston region.
* ValuJet Inc said it is receiving heavy bookings in response to its $19 introductory fares as it prepares to renew flights after being grounded for three months.
* Merrill Lynch will unveil a client-reward program that resembles frequent-flyer miles.
* Aluminum Co of America plans charges totalling $65.5 million to write down assets and cut 2,900 jobs or 3.8 percent of its work force.
